# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

content.content:
=== V2__sheet_today.sql
-- The sheet's own "today": every date decision and default date on the sheet uses it, never the
-- real clock. It starts as the real date the sheet is first loaded.
ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN today DATE;
UPDATE sheet SET today = CAST(created_at AS DATE) WHERE today IS NULL;
ALTER TABLE sheet ALTER COLUMN today SET NOT NULL;
=== V6__rate.sql
-- The sheet's rate for each grade: a percent (0.00 or more, two decimals). A grade with no row has no rate.
CREATE TABLE rate (
    sheet_id   VARCHAR(200)   NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    grade      VARCHAR(1)     NOT NULL,
    pct        DECIMAL(19, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (pct >= 0),
    set_by     VARCHAR(200)   NOT NULL,
    set_at     TIMESTAMP      NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, grade)
);
=== V14__period.sql
-- The sheet's periods: a name (unique on the sheet, compared without regard to case; stored trimmed)
-- and a from and to date, inclusive, from on or before to. No two periods on a sheet overlap (checked
-- when one is added). A claim belongs to the period whose dates contain its date, or to none.
CREATE TABLE period (
    id         BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id   VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    name       VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    name_key   VARCHAR(200) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (LOWER(name)),
    from_date  DATE         NOT NULL,
    to_date    DATE         NOT NULL,
    created_by VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    CHECK (from_date <= to_date)
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX period_sheet_name ON period (sheet_id, name_key);
CREATE INDEX period_sheet_from ON period (sheet_id, from_date);
=== V18__setting_role.sql
-- A sheet's settings, by key; a null value is blank (for clerk-limit: no limit). A key with no row is blank.
CREATE TABLE sheet_setting (
    sheet_id   VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    setting    VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    val        VARCHAR(200),
    set_by     VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    set_at     TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, setting)
);
-- The role a user name has on a sheet: clerk or steward. A name with no row is a clerk.
CREATE TABLE sheet_role (
    sheet_id   VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    user_name  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    role       VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('clerk', 'steward')),
    set_by     VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    set_at     TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, user_name)
);
=== V24__claim_due_by.sql
-- A claim's due-by, fixed when it is added: its date plus the terms of its person's grade in force on
-- its date (a grade's own terms, setting terms-<grade>, else the sheet's terms). It does not change
-- when the terms or its date change later. Claims already added take their date plus the sheet's
-- terms now (14 when never set).
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN due_by DATE;
UPDATE claim SET due_by = DATEADD(DAY, COALESCE((SELECT CAST(s.val AS INT) FROM sheet_setting s
    WHERE s.sheet_id = claim.sheet_id AND s.setting = 'terms'), 14), claim_date);
ALTER TABLE claim ALTER COLUMN due_by SET NOT NULL;
=== V27__rate_to.sql
-- A rate can carry a to-date: it applies through that date. A claim dated after the to-date of the
-- rate that would apply to it (the latest from-date on or before its date) has no rate. Null: no end.
ALTER TABLE rate ADD COLUMN to_date DATE;
=== V28__period_person_total.sql
-- A closed period's figures per person: each person on the sheet when it was closed, with the due of
-- their claims that count dated in it, fixed at that moment. A person added later has none (0.00).
-- Removed when the period is reopened. The period's due-total is the sum of these.
CREATE TABLE period_person_total (
    period_id BIGINT        NOT NULL REFERENCES period (id),
    person_id BIGINT        NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    total     DECIMAL(19, 2) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (period_id, person_id)
);
=== V29__setting_from.sql
-- A setting that carries a figure is dated: each value saved applies from its from-date, a key may
-- have several (one per from-date), and the value in force on a date is the one with the latest
-- from-date on or before it. No from-date applies from the beginning of time: the values set before
-- settings were dated, and the undated keys (policy-date, period-numbering-from).
ALTER TABLE sheet_setting ADD COLUMN from_date DATE;
ALTER TABLE sheet_setting DROP PRIMARY KEY;
ALTER TABLE sheet_setting ADD COLUMN from_key DATE GENERATED ALWAYS AS (COALESCE(from_date, DATE '0001-01-01'));
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX sheet_setting_from ON sheet_setting (sheet_id, setting, from_key);
=== V32__role_viewer.sql
-- A third role: a viewer sees everything on the sheet and may change nothing. The role check is
-- unnamed, so the table is rebuilt with the wider one.
CREATE TABLE sheet_role_new (
    sheet_id   VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    user_name  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    role       VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('clerk', 'steward', 'viewer')),
    set_by     VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    set_at     TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, user_name)
);
INSERT INTO sheet_role_new (sheet_id, user_name, role, set_by, set_at)
    SELECT sheet_id, user_name, role, set_by, set_at FROM sheet_role;
DROP TABLE sheet_role;
ALTER TABLE sheet_role_new RENAME TO sheet_role;
=== V35__delegation.sql
-- A steward delegates the steward role to a user for a from-date to a to-date, inclusive, by the
-- sheet's today. While the sheet's today is inside the range the user acts as a steward in every rule,
-- and the audit lines of a change they make name the steward who delegated (for=).
CREATE TABLE delegation (
    id           BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id     VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    user_name    VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    from_date    DATE         NOT NULL,
    to_date      DATE         NOT NULL,
    delegated_by VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    delegated_at TIMESTAMP    NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);
CREATE INDEX delegation_user ON delegation (sheet_id, user_name);
=== V39__period_soft_close.sql
-- A soft-closed period: its due-total (closed_total) and each person's figure for it
-- (period_person_total) are fixed at the moment it was soft-closed, but claims dated inside it can
-- still be added and changed. It can then be closed (fixing the figures afresh) or reopened.
ALTER TABLE period ADD COLUMN soft_closed BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
-- A claim added while the period its date falls in was soft-closed.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN late_entry BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
=== V42__sheet_snapshot.sql
-- What a sheet held each time its today changed: the sheet's rows are copied into their own schema
-- (SNAP_<id>), kept with the today they stood at (today_was) and the today set next (today_now). A
-- screen shown as of a date reads the last copy taken as the sheet's today moved past that date.
CREATE SEQUENCE sheet_snapshot_seq;
CREATE TABLE sheet_snapshot (
    id        BIGINT       PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    today_was DATE         NOT NULL,
    today_now DATE         NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX sheet_snapshot_sheet ON sheet_snapshot (sheet_id, id);
=== V69__period_cap.sql
-- The most OPEN or PENDING claims a person may have in the period (claims due by a day in it); null: no cap.
ALTER TABLE period ADD COLUMN claim_cap INT;
=== V71__rate_forward_only.sql
-- A rate saved with a from-date on or after the sheet's today is forward-only: it applies only to
-- claims added after it was saved. Its claims_after is the highest claim id there was when it was
-- saved (claims with an id up to it keep the rate that applied to them: the version it replaced, if
-- that applied to them, else none from its from-date). NULL: the rate applies to every claim.
ALTER TABLE rate ADD COLUMN claims_after BIGINT;
ALTER TABLE rate_version ADD COLUMN claims_after BIGINT;
ALTER TABLE rate_history ADD COLUMN claims_after BIGINT;
=== V79__period_opening.sql
-- A person's opening balance for a period: pasted amounts added up. It is added to their carried
-- figure for the period (and fixed with it when the period is closed or soft-closed).
CREATE TABLE period_opening (
    period_id BIGINT         NOT NULL REFERENCES period (id),
    person_id BIGINT         NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    amount    DECIMAL(19, 2) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (period_id, person_id)
);
=== V87__period_locked.sql
-- A locked period: only a steward locks and unlocks it, and while locked it cannot be reopened.
ALTER TABLE period ADD COLUMN locked BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
=== V89__sheet_source.sql
-- The sheet a clone was copied from (none: the sheet was not cloned). A grade with no rate in force on
-- a date on a clone nor on its parents takes the source's (and so on up the source's parents and source).
CREATE TABLE sheet_source (
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) PRIMARY KEY,
    source_id VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL
);
=== V72__user_locale.sql
-- Each user's locale, for themselves across every sheet: how the screen shows them figures. A user
-- with no row is en.
CREATE TABLE user_locale (
    user_name VARCHAR(200) PRIMARY KEY,
    locale    VARCHAR(10)  NOT NULL
);
=== V73__user_hidden_column.sql
-- The columns of the people list each user has switched off on a sheet, for their own screen only.
-- A column with no row is shown.
CREATE TABLE user_hidden_column (
    sheet_id    VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    user_name   VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    column_name VARCHAR(50)  NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, user_name, column_name)
);

== rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/delegations.POST.yml
# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/delegations — a steward delegates the steward role to a user for a
# from-date to a to-date (inclusive; blank: the sheet's today); refused for anyone but a steward, or a
# to-date before the from-date. A viewer may change nothing: refused before anything is read or written.
  setting.RefuseViewer
  setting.ValidateDelegation
  setting.Delegate
  setting.RecordDelegated
  setting.RespondWithDelegation
== rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/import-openings.POST.yml
# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/import-openings — add each pasted line of name,period,amount to the
# person's opening balance for the period (so to their carried figure for it). Every line is checked
# first: a person not on the sheet by name or alias, a period not on the sheet, or an amount that is not
# 0.00 or more with two decimals refuses the whole paste and nothing is written.
# Responds with how many lines went through.
# A viewer may change nothing: refused before anything is read or written.
  setting.RefuseViewer
  period.ValidateImportOpenings
  period.ImportOpenings
  period.RespondWithImportOpenings
== rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/generate-periods.POST.yml
# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/generate-periods — make one period per calendar month from the from-date's
# month to the to-date's month, leaving out a month whose name is taken or whose days overlap a period.
# A to-date before the from-date is refused. Responds with how many were made.
# A viewer may change nothing: refused before anything is read or written.
  setting.RefuseViewer
  period.GeneratePeriods
  period.RespondWithGeneratedPeriods
== rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods.POST.yml
# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods — add a period; a missing or taken name, a bad date, a from-date
# after the to-date or dates overlapping another period are refused.
# A viewer may change nothing: refused before anything is read or written.
  setting.RefuseViewer
  period.ValidatePeriod
  period.AddPeriod
  period.RecordPeriodAdded
  period.RespondWithPeriod
== rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/{name}/lock.POST.yml
# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/{name}/lock — lock a period; refused (409) for anyone but a steward,
# or when it is already locked. A locked period cannot be reopened.
  period.LockPeriod
  period.RecordPeriodLocked
  period.RespondWithPeriod
== rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/{name}/reopen.POST.yml
# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/{name}/reopen — reopen a closed or soft-closed period, making its due-total
# live again; refused (409) for anyone but a steward, or when it is neither closed nor soft-closed.
# A viewer may change nothing: refused before anything is read or written.
  setting.RefuseViewer
  period.ReopenPeriod
  period.RecordPeriodReopened
  period.RespondWithPeriod
== rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/{name}/soft-close.POST.yml
# POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/{name}/soft-close — soft-close a period, fixing its figures (claims in it stay open to change); refused
# (409) when it is already closed or soft-closed, and (403) for a role the permission matrix does not let close.
# A viewer may change nothing: refused before anything is read or written.
  setting.RefuseViewer
  period.SoftClosePeriod
  period.RecordPeriodSoftClosed
  period.RespondWithPeriod

content.text:
I read every class you listed. All paths below are relative to `/home/daniel/ui-work/runs/202610271-to/sandbox/officehq-tanstack-officefloor/src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/`.

**Conventions that apply everywhere**
- Audit lines start `EVENT sheet=<id> by=<by or "">`.
- Exception → HTTP status: `InvalidPersonException` 400 (`person/HandleInvalidPerson.java:11`), `PersonConflictException` 409 with message "Person <id> was changed by someone else" (`HandlePersonConflict.java:11`), `PersonNotFoundException` 404 "No person <id>" (`LoadPerson.java:12`). `InvalidPlanException` and `InvalidCrewException` are 400.
- "As names are compared" means `trim().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)` (`PersonRepository.java:305`), stored as `name_key`/`alias_key`.
- **Role checks:** inside these Java classes they appear only in CancelStatement, MergePerson, TransferPerson, ValidateTransferUndo, FlagPerson, BulkGrade/BulkRetire (viewer) and PasteClaims (`Permissions.OPEN`). Single hold, retire, unretire, alias, patron, approver, watch and move have no role check in Java. Any gating for those would be in the flow config, which I did not check.

---

### person/PersonRepository.java
- **list** (`:48-69`): people ordered by `list_pos, id`. Each is filled with grades, terms, holds, aliases, clashing, retirements, snapshots and statements, plus patrons ordered by `added_at, patron_id`.
- **NEXT_POS** (`:45`): `COALESCE(MAX(list_pos),0)+1`. A person added or arriving goes to the end of the list.
- **addedAfter** (`:92-95`): true when `added_on` is after the date. A null `added_on` means the person was always on the sheet.
- **findAsOf** (`:99-128`) rebuilds the person as of a date:
  - Grades: for each `from_key`, the latest `person_grade_history` row with `on_date IS NULL OR on_date <= asOf`.
  - Holds: those with `added_on IS NULL OR <= asOf`.
  - `retiredFrom`: the last `person_retired_history` row with `on_date <= asOf`.
  - Past retirements: those with `to_date <= asOf`.
  - Terms are not as-of; they are loaded current.
- **withGrades** (`:131-145`): the grade in force is worked out against `sheet.today`, falling back to `LocalDate.now()`. Grades are ordered by `from_key`, with a null from-date first.
- **withStatements** (`:209-223`): standing statements in `taken_at, id` order. A null total shows as `"n/a"`.
- **Snapshots** (`:194-229`): `person_snapshot(day_left, due_total)`.
- **treeSheets** (`:246-266`): ancestors through the `sheet_setting` row `parent`, plus all descendants, minus self and minus sheets that no longer exist. `treeNames` (`:291-298`) is every `name_key` and `alias_key` on those sheets.
- **Clashing** (`:310-317`): true when the person's name or any alias is in `treeNames`.
- **nameTaken** (`:344-350`): another person on the sheet has the name, or anyone on the sheet has it as an alias.
- **contactTaken** (`:353-358`): exact match against another person.
- **add** (`:371-400`):
  - `added_on` is the sheet's today; the person goes to the end of the list.
  - The first grade has `from_date NULL` ("from the beginning of time") and is written to grade history.
  - Tags are merged into `sheet_tag`.
- **saveGrade** (`:404-416`): replaces the grade with the same from-date and writes history with `on_date` = sheet today. **saveTerms** (`:420-426`): replaces the terms with the same from-date.
- **update** (`:436-446`): optimistic lock, `WHERE version = ?`, then `version+1`. Returns false (nothing written) on a conflict.
- **updateStatements** (`:457-461`): sets `statement_count`, `stated_total` and `statement_date` and inserts a `person_statement` row. The version does not change.
- **cancelStatement** (`:465-478`):
  - Deletes the newest `person_statement` (by id).
  - Reloads the one before it through `person.unstated(prevTotal, prevDate)`, or nulls when there is none.
  - The count goes down by one; the version does not change.
- **updateRetired** (`:488-494`): sets `retired_from` and appends `person_retired_history(on_date = today)`.
- **updateUnretired** (`:498-506`): sets `retired_from = NULL`, inserts the last `Retirement` into `person_retirement`, and appends history with `retired_from NULL`.
- **updateFlag** (`:515-518`): `flag_reason` and `flag_until`. **updateApprover** (`:509-512`).
- **addHold** (`:521-527`): `person_hold`, with `added_on` = sheet today and `held_by` = user.
- **merge** (`:535-584`):
  - from's name becomes an alias of into; from's aliases move to into.
  - from's patrons are added to into's, skipping into themselves and repeats.
  - Anyone who named from as a patron now names into. Rows are deleted first where that would be into themselves or a duplicate (`:550-554`).
  - Statements: from's rows move to into, and into's own rows are re-inserted after them so into's last stays last (`:557-565`). `into.absorbStatements(from)` then `saveStatements`.
  - Deleted for from: `person_hold`, `person_watch`, `person_grade`, `person_terms`, `person_grade_history`, `person_retired_history`, `person_retirement` (`:568-571`).
  - Plans move to into (`:573`).
  - Crews: crews from leads go to into as lead. from's crew memberships move to into, except where into is already a member or is the lead (`:576-581`).
  - The from person row is deleted.
- **transfer** (`:592-626`):

  - Person found by name or alias; otherwise "Not on the sheet: X".

### pool/PoolRepository.java (shares and cuts)
- **totalShare** (`:116-122`): sum of members with `current` (`from <= today <= to`, nulls unbounded; `:89-93`). Retired members count. `balanced` iff the total is exactly 100.00 (`FULL`, `:23`).
- **Pot** (`:109`): `settings.pot`. As of a date, it is the last `setting_history` value with `on_date <= date` (`:155-161`).
- **Cuts happen only** if pot != null AND total == 100.00. A sub-pool's pot is its cut in the parent pool, or none when that cut is empty (`:202-219`).
- **cut()** (`:228-262`):
  - If every current member is retired, all cuts are `""`.
  - A member cuts when `current && !retired && not held`. Held = a hold covering the sheet's today, as of the date (`:110-114`).
  - Each cutting member gets `pot*share/sumCuttingShares`, rounded `HALF_EVEN` to 2 decimals. Non-cutting members get 0.00.
  - The remainder (pot − sum) goes to the member with the smallest non-zero cut; on a tie, the latest added (`<=`). If no cut is non-zero, it goes to the last cutting member with a non-zero share.
  - Non-current members show `""`.
- **Crew pools** (`:168-198`):
  - id = −crewId; members are the lead first, then members in the order added.
  - Shares in hundredths of 10000: `each = 10000/n`; the lead gets `10000 − each*(n−1)`, so the remainder goes on the lead.
  - All are current. Total "100.00", balanced. No members gives "0.00", not balanced.
- **periodCuts** (`:40-67`): for every period with `to_date <= today` (ordered by `from_date, id`), the member's cut as of that period's to-date, or `""`.
- **As-of filtering:** pools, members, crews and holds by `added_on <= date` (null counts as 0001-01-01); retired from the last retired history with `on_date <= date` (`:137-152`).

  - `ALERT sheet by name= due-total=` for each person whose due-total went from ≤ the threshold (or none) to above it. Strictly `>`; only when the threshold is not null (`:117-119`).

### paste/PasteClaims.java
- **Role:** needs `Permissions.allows(OPEN)`; otherwise `ClaimStatusException("Your role may not open a claim")` (`:63-65`).
- **Pre-check of all lines** (`:68-94`):
  - Person found by name or alias; otherwise "Not on the sheet: X".
  - Date = the line's date, or `settings.entryDate`.
  - **Match**: the newest non-VOID/DELETED claim of that person with the same date and trimmed note. A DRAFT match is updated. A match that is not DRAFT is refused "The line matches a claim that is no longer a DRAFT" (`:164-180`).
  - New claim:
    - `retiredBefore(date)` is refused "The person is retired from X";
    - `dueBy = holidays.dueBy(date, settings.termsToday(person))` (business days, skipping weekends and holidays, fixed now);
    - `periods.requireOpen(dueBy)`;
    - `Corrections.check`;
    - `requireRefFree`;
    - a ref repeated within the paste (case-insensitive) is refused "The reference is repeated in the paste: X".
- **Writes** (`:98-154`):
  - Matched line: re-checks DRAFT ("No DRAFT claim of X matches the line"). If locked by another user: `ClaimLockedException("The claim is being edited by X")`.
  - Matched line with a changed amount: refused if claim lines total ≠ amount ("A claim with lines has their total as its amount: N"); `requireOpen(dueBy)`; amount edited; `CLAIM_EDITED ... person amount date <auditNumber>`.
  - New line: `claims.add`. Marked late entry if `softClosedOn(dueBy)`. `CLAIM_ADDED ... amount date <auditRef>`, plus `LATE_ENTRY ... amount date` when late.
  - Then opened as OpenClaim opens a claim: `requireFlagSteward`, `requireOpen`, `opensTo`, `requireNote`, `requireUnderCap`, then status set. Numbered with `ClaimNumbers.next` only when the result is OPEN. Event `opened.event()`, then the rollup changes.

- Constants: `SHARE = \d+(\.\d{1,2})?`, `MAX = 100.00`, `MAX_DEPTH = 3` (`:22-27`).
- Refusals:
  - "No such pool: id"; "No member named";
  - "No such person on the sheet: id"; "No such pool on the sheet: id";
  - share not matching the pattern: "A share is a percent with at most two decimals";
  - share ≤ 0 or > 100.00: "A share is more than 0.00 and at most 100.00";
  - bad date: "Not a date: X"; "The membership ends before it starts: F to T";
  - person already in the pool: "<name> is already in <pool>";
  - pool member: "<x> cannot contain itself" (cycle up the parent chain); "<x> is already a member of a pool"; `level + height(child) > 3`: "A chain of pools is at most 3 deep" (`:35-92`).
- The share is stored with `setScale(2)`.
- **Audit:** `POOL_MEMBER_ADDED sheet by pool name share [from] [to]`.

### pool/ValidatePool.java, AddPool.java
- Blank name refused "A pool needs a name"; "Already a pool: X"; "Already a crew, and so a pool: X". The name is trimmed and compared exactly.
- AddPool calls `sheets.open` and sets `added_on` to today.
- **Audit:** `POOL_ADDED sheet by name`.

### pool/PoolRepository.java (shares and cuts)
- **totalShare** (`:116-122`): sum of members with `current` (`from <= today <= to`, nulls unbounded; `:89-93`). Retired members count. `balanced` iff the total is exactly 100.00 (`FULL`, `:23`).
- **Pot** (`:109`): `settings.pot`. As of a date, it is the last `setting_history` value with `on_date <= date` (`:155-161`).
- **Cuts happen only** if pot != null AND total == 100.00. A sub-pool's pot is its cut in the parent pool, or none when that cut is empty (`:202-219`).
- **cut()** (`:228-262`):
  - If every current member is retired, all cuts are `""`.
  - A member cuts when `current && !retired && not held`. Held = a hold covering the sheet's today, as of the date (`:110-114`).
  - Each cutting member gets `pot*share/sumCuttingShares`, rounded `HALF_EVEN` to 2 decimals. Non-cutting members get 0.00.
  - The remainder (pot − sum) goes to the member with the smallest non-zero cut; on a tie, the latest added (`<=`). If no cut is non-zero, it goes to the last cutting member with a non-zero share.
  - Non-current members show `""`.
- **Crew pools** (`:168-198`):
  - id = −crewId; members are the lead first, then members in the order added.
  - Shares in hundredths of 10000: `each = 10000/n`; the lead gets `10000 − each*(n−1)`, so the remainder goes on the lead.
  - All are current. Total "100.00", balanced. No members gives "0.00", not balanced.
- **periodCuts** (`:40-67`): for every period with `to_date <= today` (ordered by `from_date, id`), the member's cut as of that period's to-date, or `""`.
- **As-of filtering:** pools, members, crews and holds by `added_on <= date` (null counts as 0001-01-01); retired from the last retired history with `on_date <= date` (`:137-152`).

### plan/*
- **ValidatePlan** (`:17-42`):
  - amount via `ClaimForm.check`; a correction (negative) is refused "A plan's amount is not negative";
  - start and end must be dates: "Not a date: X";
  - exactly one of every/day: "A plan runs either every N days or on a day of the month";
  - every must match `\d{1,9}` and be ≥ 1: "Every N days needs a whole number of at least 1";
  - day must match `\d{1,2}`, 1..31: "The day of the month is a whole number from 1 to 31";
  - "The end is before the start".
- **Plan.dates(last)** (`Plan.java:16-27`):
  - Monthly: `min(day, lengthOfMonth)` each month from the start's month; dates before the start are excluded.
  - Otherwise: start, start+every, … up to `last` inclusive.
- **GeneratePlanClaims** (`:38-74`):
  - Archived sheet refused; a viewer gets 0 and nothing is written.
  - For each plan in id order (skipped if the person is missing), `last = min(end, today)`.
  - Dates skipped: already made, or `person.retiredBefore(date)`.
  - `dueBy = holidays.dueBy(date, termsToday(person))`. A closed period means the date is silently skipped and retried next time.
  - Adds a DRAFT claim of the plan amount with an empty note; late entry if soft-closed; `recordMade`.
  - **Audit:** `CLAIM_ADDED sheet by person amount date <auditRef>` and `LATE_ENTRY ...`.
  - Result: `made`.
- **ListedPlan** (`:12-16`): the next 5 dates after today, on or before the end. `generated` = COUNT of `plan_claim` rows.
- AddPlan has no role check. **Audit:** `PLAN_ADDED sheet by name amount start (day=|every=) end`.

### crew/*
- **ValidateCrew:** "A crew needs a name"; "Already a crew: X"; "Already a pool: X"; "A crew needs a lead".
- **AddCrew:** a lead not on the sheet is refused "No such person on the sheet: id"; `sheets.open`.
  - **Audit:** `CREW_ADDED sheet by name lead=`.
- **AddCrewMember** (`:18-38`): "No such crew: id"; "No member named"; "No such person on the sheet: id"; "<name> leads <crew>"; "<name> is already in <crew>".
  - **Audit:** `CREW_MEMBER_ADDED sheet by crew name`.
- **CrewRepository.list(asOf)** (`:27-47`): filters by `added_on`. A lead who has left shows as name `""` with a null id.

### quick/*
- **ValidateQuickAdd:** "A name is required"; the amount goes through `ValidateClaim` with a blank date and note.
- **FindOrAddPerson** (`:32-51`):
  - Finds by name or alias.
  - Otherwise: refused "The name is already in use on the sheet's tree" if used elsewhere in the tree.
  - The grade is `settings.defaultGrade`.
  - Pre-checks `periods.requireOpen(dueBy(entryDate, settings.terms(grade, today)))`, which throws `PeriodClosedException`, so a claim that would be refused adds no one.
  - Then `sheets.open`, add.
  - **Audit:** `PERSON_ADDED sheet by name grade`, then the rollup changes.

### template/*
- **ValidateTemplate:** "A template needs a name"; the amount and note go through `ClaimForm.check` and are stored as normalised.
- **SaveTemplate:** `sheets.open`, then upsert by name (`ClaimTemplateRepository.java:36-44`). The amount has scale 2.
  - **Audit:** `TEMPLATE_SAVED sheet by name amount note`.
- **ValidateTemplateClaim:** "No such template: X". The claim is made from the template's current amount and note, with a blank date (the sheet's default).

### note/*
- **ValidateNote:** blank is refused with `InvalidSettingException("A note needs text")`.
- **AddNote:** `sheets.open`; `added_on` = sheet today.
- The list is newest first. In the as-of view, only notes with `added_on <= today` are shown (`NoteRepository.java:25-31`).
- **Audit:** `NOTE_ADDED sheet by text`.

### voidreason/*
- **ValidateVoidReason:** `InvalidSettingException` "A void reason needs text" / "Already a void reason: X" (exact trimmed match).
- **AddVoidReason:** `sheets.open`.
- **Audit:** `VOID_REASON_ADDED sheet by reason`.
- `VoidReasonRepository.any()` exists for checks elsewhere.

---

**Logic defined outside these files, which I did not open:** `Person.countsLive`, `countsClaimed`, `gradeOn`, `giveGrade`, `retiredBefore`, `stated`, `unstated`, `absorbStatements`, `unretire` (all in `person/Person.java`, which you have read), plus `Dues.of`, `Dues.shown`, `Late.rounding`, `Late.lateFrom`, `RateRepository.inForce`, `ClaimNumbers.next`, `OpenChecks.*` and `HolidayRepository.dueBy`.
